item.title: Broadcom and other AI stocks lift Wall Street closer to its record
item.description: Stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry are leading Wall Street higher on Tuesday, as their yo-yo moves swing back upward.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — Stocks in the artificial intelligence industry led Wall Street higher on Tuesday, as their yo-yo moves swing back upward. The S&P 500 rose 0.6 per cent and pulled within 1.2 per cent of its all-time high set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 15 points, or less than 0.1 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 1.2 per cent. The majority of stocks within the S&P 500 fell, but the gains for influential AI stocks made up for that. AI stocks rose to another winning day after swerving for weeks on worries about whether their boom is under threat because of how expensive it’s become for companies to borrow money to build data centers and buy more AI chips. Broadcom climbed 4 per cent after announcing a US$63 billion financing deal where several Wall Street firms will help Anthropic get access to Broadcom’s XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions. Elsewhere in the industry, Nvidia added 0.9 per cent and was one of the strongest forces behind Broadcom pushing the S&P 500 higher. CoreWeave, a company that’s borrowed money to buy AI chips that it rents out to customers over the cloud, jumped 7.9 per cent and was consistently higher through the day following several days of sharp swings. General Motors climbed 5.5 per cent after saying it’s moving its stock from a listing on the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq. The automaker said the Nasdaq, which is home to several of the world’s biggest technology stocks, is a fit for its tech-driven strategy. The move could also allow GM to join the Nasdaq 100 index, which would force investment funds that mimic the index to buy it. GM began trading on the NYSE in 1911. JetBlue Airways flew 19 per cent higher even though it reported a larger loss for the summer than analysts expected. CEO Joanna Geraghty said the company expects to return to making sustained operating profits next year and to deliver at least US$1 in earnings per share in 2028. Investors may have been bracing for something worse after the airline’s stock came into the day with a loss of nearly 48 per cent for the year so far. Another travel company, Royal Caribbean Group, also helped lead the market and rose 5.5 per cent. The cruise operator delivered a stronger profit for the summer than analysts expected, while raising its forecast for profit over the full year. Companies overall are under pressure to deliver big growth in profits. Expectations are high among financial analysts and investors, and that’s what allowed their stock prices to run to records recently despite high inflation, high interest rates and other concerns weighing on the market. Boeing fell 10.7 per cent after reporting a larger loss for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Hilton Worldwide Holdings sank 2.1 per cent after reporting weaker revenue for the summer than analysts expected. It also gave a range as a forecast for profit in the final three months of the year whose midpoint fell below analysts’ expectations. The hotel company said it expects to see “increased impact from the Middle East” during the quarter. Sherwin-Williams fell 2.7 per cent after delivering a weaker profit than analysts expected. High mortgage rates have chilled the housing industry, which in turn pressures demand for the paints and coatings Sherwin-Williams sells. “Customer sentiment and the leading indicators we track point to muted demand over the remainder of the year and into 2027,” CEO Heidi Petz said. At the same time, her company is dealing with inflation pushing up its costs for raw materials. Confidence among U.S. shoppers has tumbled recently as pressure keeps building on them from high inflation. But a report on Tuesday said that U.S. consumer confidence improved in October, when economists expected further weakening. All told, the S&P 500 rose 45.83 points to 7,722.60. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 15.99 to 52,377.57, and the Nasdaq composite rallied 308.43 to 26,477.81. In the bond market, U.S. Treasury yields held relatively steady a day before the U.S. Federal Reserve is scheduled to announce its latest decision on interest rates. The Fed last month hiked the fed funds rate for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing inflation, but the widespread expectation on Wall Street is that it will hold rates steady this time. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged down to 4.99 per cent from 5.00 per cent late Monday. Helping to keep yields in check was a drop for oil prices. The price for a barrel of Brent crude fell 1.2 per cent to US$109.41. In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed across Europe and Asia. Stocks jumped 3.1 per cent in Seoul and fell 1.3 per cent in Shanghai for two of the bigger moves. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Writers Elaine Lai and Matt Ott contributed to this report.

item.title: TMX CEO wants to see Canadian capital markets compete on world stage
item.description: The chief executive of TMX Group Ltd. says he’d like to see reduced regulatory and cost barriers for companies wanting to list on Canada’s main stock exchange as it looks to gain a competitive edge ...
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: CALGARY — The chief executive of TMX Group Ltd. says he’d like to see reduced regulatory and cost barriers for companies wanting to list on Canada’s main stock exchange as it looks to gain a competitive edge globally. At a conference hosted by the Alberta Securities Commission, John McKenzie was asked whether he is concerned about the drop in numbers of issuers trading on the TSX. McKenzie says it’s not a phenomenon that’s limited to Canada and that it’s partly a function of there being so much growth concentrated in a relatively few large-cap names. He says it’s good to have Canadian heavyweights that are able to compete on the world stage, but he also wants to see small- and medium-cap names thrive and scale up, too. He says the tax and regulatory burden that applies to a major multibillion-dollar company like Enbridge Inc., for example, shouldn’t also have to be shouldered by a $20-million firm with fewer resources. McKenzie says for the first nine months of the year, TMX brought more than 300 new issuers into the market — two-thirds structured products and one-third companies. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 27, 2026. Lauren Krugel, The Canadian Press

item.content:encoded:
Barry Schwartz, President & CIO, Baskin Wealth Management Focus: North American Large Caps

Top Picks: TFI International , Fairfax , Topicus.com MARKET OUTLOOK: In a market where not much is working, it is tempting to sell your stocks that have done nothing and chase performance. This is the absolute wrong approach in our opinion. Now more than ever, investors should be diversifying their portfolios especially given a very concentrated market in artificial intelligence (AI) names in the U.S. For AI, we favour they hyperscalers that we think will start showing tremendous free cash flow in 2028 and beyond. We think there are lots of good opportunities in predictable and durable businesses that are perceived to be AI losers. How to set BNN Bloomberg as your preferred source on Google Market-moving news, fast:  Get the BNN Bloomberg App now Sign up for the Market Call Top Picks newsletter at  bnnbloomberg.ca/newsletters TOP PICKS: Barry Schwartz's Top Picks: TFI International, Fairfax & Topicus.com Barry Schwartz, president & CIO at Baskin Wealth Management, shares his top stock picks to watch in the market.

TFI International (TFII TSX) Trucking sector is currently volatile: sluggish economic activity outside of data centers, uncertainty from tariffs, but tight driver supply leading to higher trucking rates. Recent court ruling on broker liability will benefit large operators like TFI Generates strong free cash flows throughout the cycle due to their asset-light model… has been repurchasing stock in 2025, and likely doing so again with the dip Has M&A opportunities in all of their divisions, could still spin-off the truckload division in the future as well. Longer-term, will benefit from autonomous trucks. Trades at about 12x free cash flow… well under other LTL peers like ODFL. Fairfax (FFH TSX) Stock has been weak due to worries about a soft market for insurance. Fairfax focuses on global, specialty lines which should be more resilient than North American P&C lines and will likely generate an underwriting profit this year. Will benefit from higher interest rates… has deliberately kept their fixed income portfolio short duration (under 4 years) Is active on investing: participated in Boots takeover with the Weston family, and acquired a stake in an Indian bank (IBDI) Stock is extremely cheap at 1.2 times book value and under nine times earnings. Topicus.com (TOI TSX) Constellation Software affiliate focused on Europe. Is resilient to AI due to local regulations in Europe such as language requirements. Needs to be a local provider in many cases. Has had a relatively light year of acquisitions and some leadership change with CEO Robin van Poelje retiring. Stock has underperformed Constellation Software and is now trading at a cheaper multiple despite historically having faster organic growth.
